chunks: In the narration of Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:

He was asked about a man who had a wife, then committed zina with her mother, her daughter, or her sister. So he said: “An unlawful act has never made a lawful thing unlawful. His wife is lawful for him.”

And he said: “There is no harm, if a man commits zina with a woman, in marrying her afterward.” He gave the example of that as the example of a man who stole a date from a palm tree, then bought it afterward. “And there is no harm in his marrying afterward her mother, her daughter, or her sister. And if the woman is under him, then he marries her mother, her daughter, or her sister and enters upon her, then later comes to know, he separates from the latter, while the first is his wife. And he must not approach his wife until the womb of the one from whom he separated is cleared. And if a man commits zina with his son’s wife, or his father’s wife, or his son’s slave-girl, or his father’s slave-girl, then that does not make her unlawful for her husband, nor does the slave-girl become unlawful for her master. Rather, that only makes it unlawful when that was by him with the slave-girl while she was lawful for him; then that slave-girl is never lawful for his son nor for his father. And when he marries a woman in a lawful marriage, then that woman is not lawful for his son nor for his father.”

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: a slave-girl/concubine in the legal context of the hadith
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman or wife discussed in the ruling
key_terms.تَزْوِيجًا: marriage contract in a lawful form
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: an unlawful act, here referring to zina and its legal status
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: lawful or permissible in marital and sexual relations
key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئَ: to ensure the womb is cleared before resuming relations

ai.seo_question: Does committing zina with a woman or her relatives make a lawful wife unlawful in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on whether zina affects the permissibility of existing or later marital relations. It states that an unlawful act does not itself invalidate a lawful marriage, while also clarifying the permanent prohibitions that arise through lawful sexual relations and lawful marriage.
